name: Zermatt
tagline: Car-free alpine village beneath the unmistakable Matterhorn
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Sep, Oct, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: January to March for snow-sure skiing under the Matterhorn, July to August for high-alpine hiking. Shoulder weeks bring quiet and some lift closures.

ourTake.lede: Zermatt is car-free and all about the Matterhorn, so the game is catching the mountain in clear light, the peak often clouds by late morning, so be up early. Take the Gornergrat railway at dawn for the classic view, and ride to the highest station in Europe at Matterhorn Glacier Paradise. The village itself is charming but the reason to come is above 3,000 metres.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a car-free Alpine village with the Matterhorn at your window and grand-hotel comfort.
ourTake.skipIf: You want warmth, a beach or a low bill.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Mont Cervin Palace
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: The 1852 grande dame at the heart of the village, the address Zermatt is measured against.

items.name: Riffelalp Resort 2222m
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: Europe's highest five-star hotel, car-free, reached only by the Gornergrat railway, alone with the Matterhorn.

items.name: Grand Hotel Zermatterhof
items.description: A Belle Époque palace built by the villagers themselves in 1879, old-world grandeur, impeccably kept.

items.name: The Omnia
items.description: A minimalist mountain lodge on the rock above the village, reached by a tunnel and lift cut into the mountainside.

items.name: CERVO Mountain Resort
items.description: A cluster of chalets at the foot of the Sunnegga slopes, sustainable, stylish and quietly modern.

items.name: Backstage Hotel Vernissage
credentials: Home of After Seven, 2 MICHELIN Stars
items.description: Artist Heinz Julen's avant-garde design hotel, sculptural, theatrical and unlike anything else in the Alps.

items.name: Gornergrat Railway
credentials: Highest open-air cogwheel railway in Europe
items.description: The cogwheel train that hauls you from the village up to 3,089m in about 33 minutes, and the whole way the Matterhorn hangs in the window over a fan of glaciers and 4,000m peaks. Book seats on the right for the best of it, and let the little ones and the grandparents ride effortlessly to a view most people only earn on foot. This is the single easiest, most magnificent multi-generation morning in the Alps.

items.name: Gornergrat summit & Kulmhotel observatory
credentials: Views of 29 peaks above 4,000m including Monte Rosa, the highest in Switzerland
items.description: The top station is a natural balcony ringed by 29 peaks over 4,000m and the vast Gorner Glacier, with the astronomical observatory domes of the Kulmhotel crowning the ridge. The air is thin and the silence total; a private guide can name every summit while you sip something warm. Come for the panorama, stay for the astonishing near-zero-light-pollution night sky.

items.name: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise
items.description: The highest cable-car station on the continent, where a viewing platform opens onto 38 four-thousanders and 14 glaciers spread across Switzerland, Italy and France. The lift does all the climbing; you simply step out into the roof of Europe. For an Indian family, it is the closest thing to standing on top of the Alps without a rope.

items.name: The Glacier Palace ice cave
credentials: World's highest glacier ice palace (inside the 3,883m station)
items.description: A tunnel carved fifteen metres into the living glacier, walls of blue ice, carved sculptures, and a small ice slide the children will beg to repeat. It sits inside the highest cable-car station in Europe, so you fold it into the summit visit. Wrap up warm; the cave holds a steady sub-zero even in a July heatwave.

items.name: The Cinema Lounge, Klein Matterhorn
items.description: A small cinema at nearly 3,900m showing short films on the mountains, the glacier and the flora, a gentle place to acclimatise and rest while the body adjusts to the altitude. It is an easy, warm interlude for grandparents between the ice cave and the platform. A quiet reminder that even the roof of Europe can be done in comfort.

items.name: Matterhorn Glacier Ride (3S cableway)
items.description: The tri-cable gondola that lifts you the final stretch to the summit station in nine minutes, crystal-studded 'Crystal ride' cabins with glass floors on select cabins that turn transparent over the glacier. It is a thrill in itself, engineering as spectacle. Ask about the crystal cabin for a set-piece the teenagers will film the whole way up.

items.name: Matterhorn Alpine Crossing to Cervinia
credentials: Highest cross-border cable-car crossing in the Alps
items.description: Since 2023 you can ride cable cars clear over the ridge from Zermatt into Italy, lunch in Breuil-Cervinia, and glide back, the highest year-round border crossing in the Alps done entirely by gondola, no climbing, no passports checked mid-air but carry yours. Two countries and a plate of pasta on the Italian sun-terrace, all in an afternoon. A brilliant, effortless multi-country day.

items.name: Riffelsee & the Matterhorn reflection
items.description: Step off the cogwheel train at Rotenboden and a short walk brings you to the Riffelsee, the small tarn that gives the picture-postcard mirror image of the Matterhorn on a still morning. It is the most photographed reflection in the Alps and the reason to catch the earliest train. A calm, windless dawn is everything, so time it with your guide.

items.name: Gornergrat sunrise & Riffelsee special train
items.description: On set dates the railway runs a dedicated pre-dawn service so you reach the ridge as the first light turns the Matterhorn's east face to fire and doubles it in the Riffelsee. Breakfast follows at the mountain restaurant while the crowds are still asleep in the valley. Pure honeymoon material, and worth the early alarm.

items.name: Five Lakes Walk (5-Seenweg)
items.description: A gentle high trail past five alpine lakes, Stellisee, Grindjisee, Grünsee, Moosjisee and Leisee, three of which mirror the Matterhorn on a calm day. No exposure, no scrambling, just larch forest, wildflowers and one perfect reflection after another over three to four hours. The most rewarding easy hike above Zermatt for a mixed-ability family.

items.name: Stellisee lake
items.description: The wind-sheltered jewel of the Five Lakes Walk and, for many, the finest Matterhorn reflection of all, an unbroken double of the peak on a still summer morning. The Fluhalp mountain restaurant sits a few minutes on for a leisurely lunch with the same view. Go early; by midday a breeze usually ruffles the mirror.

items.name: Sunnegga & Leisee
items.description: A three-minute underground funicular from the village lifts you to a sunny terrace and the shallow Leisee, a warm-ish swimming lake with the Matterhorn behind and a lakeside playground, the gentlest of the high viewpoints. Perfect for a family with young children or grandparents who want the view without the walk. The quickest route from village to a first Matterhorn panorama.

items.name: Rothorn viewpoint
items.description: The highest of the Sunnegga-side summits, reached by funicular and cable car, with a wide sweep of glaciers and a superb, less-crowded angle on the Matterhorn. It is a spectacular sunrise perch for those who want the golden peak without the Gornergrat crowds. A quiet counterpoint to the busier railway summit.

items.name: Matterhorn Museum – Zermatlantis
items.description: An underground reconstructed old village that tells how a poor farming hamlet became the world's most famous mountain, centred on the snapped rope from the 1865 first ascent that killed four of Edward Whymper's seven climbers. Whymper's ice-axe and boots, the church bells, the cobbled lanes, it is moving and beautifully done. The one indoor hour that makes the whole valley make sense.

items.name: The Hinterdorf old village
items.description: A cluster of black larch barns, stables and granaries from the 16th to 18th centuries, many raised on stilts topped with round flat 'mouse-stones' to keep rodents out of the grain. A five-minute wander back through Walliser mountain life, wedged among the boutiques. Loveliest in late light when the resinous timber glows almost black.

items.name: The Kirchbrücke (church bridge) view
items.description: The little bridge over the Matter Vispa where the whole village funnels the eye straight up to the Matterhorn, the classic street-level shot with chalets, church tower and peak all in one frame. It is a two-minute stroll from the grand hotels and best at first light or blue hour. The picture everyone comes home with.

items.name: Bahnhofstrasse & luxury shopping
items.description: The car-free main street lined with Swiss watch houses and jewellers, Bucherer for Rolex, Patek, Chopard and Cartier, alongside ski and cashmere boutiques and chocolatiers. No cars, no fumes, just electric taxis and the Matterhorn at the end of the road. An elegant, unhurried afternoon between mountain excursions.

items.name: The car-free village stroll
credentials: One of Europe's original car-free (combustion-free) resorts
items.description: Zermatt has banned petrol cars for decades; you arrive by train and move by foot, e-taxi or horse-drawn sleigh, and the air is clean and the streets quiet. That exclusivity, an entire luxury village without traffic, is a large part of its charm for a discerning traveller. Simply walking it in the evening, watching the peak turn pink, is an event in itself.

items.name: Gorner Gorge (Gornerschlucht)
items.description: A narrow slot canyon of 220-million-year-old green serpentine rock, threaded by a timber walkway first built by local guides in the 1880s, with turquoise meltwater roaring below. Fifteen minutes from the centre and blessedly cool on a hot day. A short, dramatic detour that suits a rainy morning or restless children.

items.name: Mountaineers' Cemetery
items.description: A small, sobering graveyard where climbers who died on the Matterhorn and Monte Rosa lie, including victims of the 1865 first ascent, headstones carved with ropes, axes and 'I chose to climb'. It is quiet and dignified, a few minutes from the busy street. A poignant counterweight to the glamour, and part of understanding this mountain.

items.name: Chez Vrony, Findeln
items.description: The most coveted mountain table above Zermatt, a century-old family farm-restaurant on a sun-terrace facing the Matterhorn, serving its own dry-cured meats, alpine cheese and a famous burger from cattle grazed on the slope. Book well ahead; the terrace at lunch is where Zermatt's regulars are. An unhurried, glorious high-altitude lunch with the peak for a backdrop.

items.name: Findeln hamlet & its restaurants
items.description: A scatter of old timber chalets, a tiny chapel and a run of celebrated mountain restaurants, Findlerhof, Adler and others, strung across a south-facing slope twenty minutes' walk below Sunnegga. Larch, cowbells and the Matterhorn framed between the barns. The prettiest lunch-walk in the resort, gentle enough for most.

items.name: Fondue & raclette in the village
items.description: This is the Valais, the home of raclette, and a bubbling caquelon of fondue or a scraped wheel of alpine cheese in a low-beamed stube is the evening ritual after a day on the heights. Ask ahead and the better kitchens will do a fine vegetarian spread, cheese, potatoes, pickles, rösti, that suits Indian tastes well. Warm, convivial and utterly of the place.

items.name: Zermatt–Cervinia international ski area
items.description: One of the largest linked ski areas in the Alps, spanning two countries, over 300km of pistes and lifts to 3,883m, so you can ski down to lunch in Italy and be back in Switzerland by tea. Long, sun-soaked, high-altitude runs with the Matterhorn always in view. A private ski guide and ski-in ski-out chalet make it seamless for a family.

items.name: Summer glacier skiing
credentials: Highest and largest summer ski area in the Alps
items.description: The Matterhorn Glacier Paradise pistes let you ski or snowboard on real snow through July and August, a novelty few places on earth can offer, then swap boots for sandals in the valley the same day. Ideal for a summer-visiting family who want their children to touch snow in high season. The highest, largest summer ski area in the Alps.

items.name: Heli-skiing with Air Zermatt
items.description: One of only a handful of legal heli-ski zones in Switzerland, where the storied Air Zermatt lifts you to untracked glacier faces such as the Monte Rosa for a guided descent through deep powder. It is the ultimate winter adrenaline day, private, exclusive and framed by the Matterhorn. For confident skiers, nothing here comes close.

items.name: Climbing the Matterhorn (guided)
credentials: First climbed 1865 by Edward Whymper's party; four of seven died on descent
items.description: The bucket-list ascent, a serious two-day climb via the Hörnli hut with a Zermatt IFMGA guide one-to-one, demanding real fitness and prior alpine experience. Even if you never rope up, standing at the Hörnli hut base and watching the dawn summit attempts is unforgettable. For the right guest, this is the summit of a lifetime; for the rest, its story is the soul of the village.

items.name: Schwarzsee & the Maria zum Schnee chapel
items.description: A cable car ride to a small dark lake with a lonely white pilgrimage chapel and the Matterhorn looming directly above, close enough to feel its scale. On a still day the chapel and peak double in the water. It is also the gateway to the Hörnli hut trail, so climbers and photographers cross paths here.

items.name: The Matterhorn Glacier Trail
items.description: A well-graded high path beneath the Matterhorn's east face, past glacial lakes, information panels on the 1865 ascent and the retreating ice, with the peak looming the whole way. Around two hours, moderate, and endlessly photogenic. A serious Matterhorn hike that stays within reach of most fit walkers.

items.name: Riffelalp Resort & Europe's highest tram
items.description: A five-star mountain resort on the Gornergrat line with a 35°C open-air pool facing the Matterhorn and a little red tram, the highest in Europe, trundling guests from the station to the door. Even non-residents can ride up for the terrace and the spa's altitude drama. A honeymoon set-piece and a rare high-altitude luxury address.

items.name: Paragliding over Zermatt
items.description: A tandem flight that floats you off the shoulder of the mountain and out in front of the Matterhorn itself, twenty minutes of silent, soaring perspective no cable car can give. First-timers are strapped to a seasoned pilot; the harder part is the view, not the flying. An exhilarating hour for an adventurous couple or teenager.

items.name: E-biking & mountain biking
items.description: Marked trails for every level, from a gentle e-bike Glacier Garden loop to the technical Rothorn descent, with lifts that carry your bike up so you only ride the good bits. The Flower Trail rolls through larch woods thick with edelweiss and gentian back to Sunnegga. A fresh, active way to see the high meadows in summer.

items.name: Ibex & chamois watching
items.description: The rocky ridges above Sunnegga are home to alpine ibex with their great curved horns and nimble chamois, often spotted early or late along the higher trails. A guide with a scope will find them and tell you the mountain's natural history. A quiet thrill for children and grandparents alike, wildlife against a Matterhorn backdrop.

items.name: Alpine flora & the Flower Trail
items.description: In high summer the meadows blaze with edelweiss, gentian, alpine rose and dozens more species along a signed flower trail that winds gently down through larch and stone pine to Sunnegga. Easy underfoot and quietly beautiful, a botanist's and a photographer's walk. A soft, unhurried counterpoint to the big summits.

items.name: The Glacier Express to St Moritz
credentials: Runs onto the UNESCO-listed Rhaetian Railway (Albula/Bernina) line
items.description: The famously slow panoramic train that threads eight hours of Alpine grandeur, 291 bridges and the Landwasser viaduct, from Zermatt to St Moritz through the UNESCO Rhaetian Railway landscape. Book the Excellence Class for a single-seat-at-the-window, five-course, sommelier-served journey. One of the world's great rail experiences, and a superb way to leave or arrive.

items.name: Sunset on the Matterhorn from the village
items.description: In the last minutes of the day the peak catches an alpenglow that runs from gold to deep rose while the valley falls into shadow, best watched from the church bridge or a south-facing hotel terrace with a drink in hand. It happens every clear evening and never tires. The most reliable free spectacle in the resort.

items.name: Mont Cervin Palace
items.description: The grande dame of Zermatt, open since 1852 and a Leading Hotel of the World, whose sun-terrace on the main street is the village's social heart and whose kitchens include a Michelin-starred Italian table. Even for a drink or afternoon tea it is worth stepping inside for the old-world grandeur. The classic address for a traveller who wants the establishment choice.

items.name: THE OMNIA design hotel
items.description: A glass-and-timber mountain lodge set on a rock 45m above the village, reached by a lift bored up through the cliff, all clean lines, fireplaces and a Michelin-recognised kitchen. Its terrace hangs over the rooftops with the Matterhorn dead ahead. The design-led, intimate alternative to the grand palace hotels, and a honeymooners' favourite.

items.name: CERVO Mountain Resort
items.area: Above the village, by the Sunnegga funicular
items.description: A cluster of chic alpine chalets with a buzzing après terrace, a superb spa and a pan-Asian and Mediterranean dining scene that draws a younger, stylish crowd. Ski-in ski-out in winter, a design-forward retreat in summer. The most fashionable stay in Zermatt for guests who want energy as well as views.

items.name: Private chalet stays
items.description: Zermatt has some of the Alps' finest catered chalets, staffed with private chef, driver and in-house spa, giving a large family or group total privacy with the Matterhorn from the hot tub. Many arrange guide, heli and restaurant bookings as part of the stay. The natural choice for multi-generational or celebration travel.

items.name: Riffelberg & its little chapel
items.description: A mid-station on the cogwheel railway with a broad terrace, a tiny chapel set perfectly beneath the peak for scale, and gentle walks down toward Riffelalp through the flowers. A relaxed, less-strenuous stop for those breaking the Gornergrat journey. The chapel-and-mountain composition is a quiet favourite of photographers.

items.name: Trockener Steg & the Theodul Glacier
items.description: The great glacier junction where the cable cars change for the summit, ringed by the Theodul Glacier and a small lake that mirrors the Matterhorn's western flank. It is the staging point for summer skiing and the Italy crossing, worth a pause for the raw glacial scale. A window on the ice for those who go no higher.

items.name: Zermatt in high summer wildflower season
items.description: July and August turn the alpine pastures into a carpet of colour under snow-streaked peaks, with long warm days, quiet trails and the mountains at their most inviting, ideal for Indian families travelling in the summer holidays. Snow up top, wildflowers below, and the Matterhorn clear against blue. The valley at its most generous.

items.name: A guided Monte Rosa excursion
credentials: Monte Rosa is the highest massif in Switzerland (Dufourspitze 4,634m)
items.description: For strong walkers, a guided crossing of the Gorner Glacier toward the striking crystalline Monte Rosa hut is a genuine high-alpine adventure without the technicality of the Matterhorn. Roped up, crampons on, you feel the scale of Switzerland's highest massif underfoot. A serious mountain day for the fit and curious, arranged privately.

items.name: Winter horse-drawn sleigh & village nights
items.description: With no cars, winter evenings belong to horse-drawn sleighs jingling through snow-lined lanes, lantern light on the old chalets and the peak silvered by the moon. A short ride to dinner or simply around the village is pure alpine romance. The car-free hush makes Zermatt's winter unlike anywhere else.

items.name: After Seven
items.description: Ivo Adam's surprise menu cooked in an open kitchen, bread baked at your table, and the village's brightest star.

items.name: The Omnia
items.description: Alpine ingredients with a global hand, in the design hotel's cool dining room on the rock above the village.

items.name: Brasserie Lusi
items.description: The Zermatterhof's confident brasserie, grand-hotel cooking without the ceremony.

items.name: Chez Vrony
items.description: A century-old family alp above the village, cooking its own organic beef with the Matterhorn full in the window.

items.name: Findlerhof
items.description: The other beloved Findeln kitchen, sun-terrace mountain cooking, refined and warmly run.

items.name: Marmo
items.description: A modern mountain kitchen at Furi, a serious table on the slopes, not just a hut.

items.name: Bazaar
items.description: Predominantly vegetarian world flavours, Arab to Chinese, at CERVO's lively base.

items.name: Aroleid Restaurant
items.description: Seasonal, honest cooking that quietly won the village's only Bib Gourmand, value done right.

items.name: Elsie's Bar
items.description: A tiny champagne-and-wine room opposite the church, in an 1879 house, the chic address since 1961.

items.name: CERVO Bar & Terrace
credentials: Within CERVO Mountain Resort, Design Hotels (Marriott Bonvoy)
items.description: A two-level slope-side terrace at the foot of Sunnegga, cocktails, DJ sets and the day's best après crowd.

items.name: Vernissage Bar
credentials: Within Backstage Hotel Vernissage, MICHELIN Guide Hotel
items.description: Heinz Julen's cinema-cum-gallery-cum-bar, sculptural, candlelit and unlike any other room in the Alps.

items.name: Hennu Stall
credentials: World Snow Awards, Zermatt named Best Après-Ski
items.description: The legendary slope-side après barn, Jägermeister on skis, Europop and fancy dress until the light goes.

plan.heading: 3 days in Zermatt, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The train in from Täsch, cars stay behind, and a slow settle into the village, the mountain filling the end of every street.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The walk up to the Gornergrat cog railway, or simply the church square and the old Hinterdorf timber barns.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at the After Seven in the Backstage Hotel, Zermatt's Michelin-starred table, then a nightcap at the Vernissage bar.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: First lift to Gornergrat for the Monte Rosa and the glacier at sunrise, coffee at the summit.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Five Lakes walk down, the Matterhorn mirrored in the Stellisee.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A mountain dinner at Chez Vrony in Findeln, arriving on foot or by rail, then down as the peaks turn.

days.label: Day 3
days.title: The glacier and a long lunch

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The cable car to the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise, Europe's highest, and the ice palace.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A long table at the Chetzeron restaurant or a spa afternoon at the Mont Cervin Palace.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final dinner at the Restaurant Schäferstube for the lamb, close and warm before departure.

items.name: Village centre (Bahnhofstrasse)
items.description: The car-free heart with the grand hotels and shops, everything on foot.

items.name: Winkelmatten
items.description: A quiet hamlet on the edge with Matterhorn views, for seclusion near the pistes.

items.name: Riffelalp
items.description: Up the mountain at 2,200m, for those who want to stay in the high alpine, above the crowds.

events.name: Zermatt Unplugged
events.note: An acoustic music festival across village and mountain stages, the 2026 edition runs 7–11 April.

events.name: Zermatt Marathon
events.note: A punishing summer run climbing from the valley up towards the Matterhorn.

events.name: Folklore Festival
events.note: Alpine traditions, yodelling and flag-throwing fill the car-free streets in high summer.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: The village sits at roughly 1,600m and peaks reach far higher, so pace the first day and hydrate; stay slopeside near the Matterhorn view, a room facing the peak is worth requesting specifically.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Zermatt is car-free, so you arrive by private car or helicopter to Täsch and transfer by the short cog railway or a resort electric shuttle up to the village beneath the Matterhorn.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: Everything moves on foot or by silent electric taxi and hotel e-buggy; the mountain railways and cable cars carry you up to the slopes and viewpoints.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Village and valley coverage is strong; an eSIM works well, and hotel wifi is reliable though it thins high on the mountain.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Swiss francs (CHF); cards are accepted across the village, carry a little cash for small mountain huts, and tipping is modest.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: December to March for reliable snow and skiing under the Matterhorn; July to September for clear hiking weather. Late April to May is the shoulder low, when many lifts and hotels close for maintenance.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Fly into Zurich (direct on SWISS or Air India from Delhi, ~8h45), then about 3.5 hours by rail with one easy change at Visp. Zermatt is car-free, so arrange the electric-taxi or hotel transfer from the station; private cars stop at Tasch, 7 km below.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required; the village is very safe. Zermatt sits at ~1,600 m and excursions like Gornergrat (3,089 m) and the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise (3,883 m) reach real altitude, so ascend gradually, hydrate, and rest on arrival. Tap water is pure.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: A resort village, so dedicated Indian dining is limited, but hotels and mountain restaurants readily handle vegetarian requests. For strict Jain meals, ask your hotel to prepare in advance or stock a few essentials before arrival.
